title: Naive cotangent complex and smooth ring maps
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Let $R[S]$ be the polynomial ring over $R$ with one variable $[s]$ for every $s\in S$, let $\gamma:R[S]\to S$ be the surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras with $\gamma([s])=s$, and $I=\ker\gamma$. The *naive cotangent complex* $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}$ is the two-term complex of $S$-modules $I/I^2\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }\bigoplus_{s\in S}S\,\mathrm d[s]$ (with $I/I^2$ in homological degree $1$ and the free $S$-module on the symbols $\mathrm d[s]$ in degree $0$), where $\delta(g\bmod I^2)=\sum_{s\in S}\gamma\bigl(\partial g/\partial[s]\bigr)\,\mathrm d[s]$ ($\partial/\partial[s]$ the formal partial derivative of $R[S]$ over $R$; $I/I^2$ is an $S=R[S]/I$-module and $\delta$ is well defined and $S$-linear by the Leibniz rule). Its homology in degree $1$ is the $S$-module $H_1(L_{S/R}):=\ker\delta$. The ring map $\varphi$ (or the $R$-algebra $S$) is *smooth* if (i) $S$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra ($S\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_m)$ as $R$-algebras for some $n,m\ge0$), (ii) $H_1(L_{S/R})=0$, and (iii) the module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{S/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a finite projective $S$-module (a direct summand of a finite free $S$-module).
